question: How many new-mover leads are in Lancaster County?
html:
New-Mover Leads in Lancaster County

The context has no Lancaster-only new-mover count. The ad plan reports new movers only for the whole nine-county PA core (about 2,300 sales a month) and the Jersey Shore. A Lancaster figure needs the county deed records split out by county (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What the data shows

  • County deed records show about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core. The Jersey Shore adds about 1,150 (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Lancaster is one of the nine core counties, alongside York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams and Perry (Punctual Pros market profile).
  • One in three PA core buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan). That share is not broken out for Lancaster.
  • The plan assumes a 1.0% lead rate per mail piece. This is deliberately below ANA prospect response of 4-5% (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Households versus leads

These are different numbers. A sale is a household that needs a provider. A lead is a household that responds to mail.

ScopeNew-mover households / monthMail leads / month at 1.0%
PA core (9 counties)~2,300~23 (est.)
Jersey Shore~1,150~11-12 (est.)
Lancaster CountyNot in contextNot in context

Lancaster's share of the core could be pro-rated by households. That would still be a guess, because Lancaster's household count and sales volume are not in the context provided.

Adjacent signal: new construction

  • Census permits for August 2026 show 124 units in Lancaster County. Of these, 48 were single-family and 72 were in buildings of five or more units (Census building permits).
  • New-build owners are a separate audience from deed-record movers. Do not add them to the mover count.

Caveat on the lead rate

  • The 1.0% rate is an assumption. It is not a measured result.
  • The week-two mail drop and the week-four read will give Punctual Pros' own response rate (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The plan also holds out 10% of new movers, so measured leads should be read against that holdout.

Next actions

  1. Pull the last 12 months of Lancaster County deed records, filtered to arm's-length residential sales. Report the monthly count and the pre-1980 share.
  2. Repeat the same split for all nine core counties. Mail volume and budget can then be allocated by county instead of across the whole core.
  3. Replace the assumed 1.0% lead rate with booked jobs per piece from mail drop one. Use ServiceTitan tracking numbers and QR codes, and compare against the holdout.
  4. Decide whether new-construction owners get a separate mail track. Lancaster's 48 single-family permits in August 2026 make that a small test, not a core list.
markdown:
# New-Mover Leads in Lancaster County

The context has no Lancaster-only new-mover count. The ad plan reports new movers only for the whole nine-county PA core (about 2,300 sales a month) and the Jersey Shore. A Lancaster figure needs the county deed records split out by county (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What the data shows

- County deed records show about 2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core. The Jersey Shore adds about 1,150 (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Lancaster is one of the nine core counties, alongside York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams and Perry (Punctual Pros market profile).
- One in three PA core buyers bought a pre-1980 home (Punctual Pros ad plan). That share is not broken out for Lancaster.
- The plan assumes a 1.0% lead rate per mail piece. This is deliberately below ANA prospect response of 4-5% (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## Households versus leads

These are different numbers. A sale is a household that needs a provider. A lead is a household that responds to mail.

| Scope | New-mover households / month | Mail leads / month at 1.0% |
|---|---|---|
| PA core (9 counties) | ~2,300 | ~23 (est.) |
| Jersey Shore | ~1,150 | ~11-12 (est.) |
| Lancaster County | Not in context | Not in context |

Lancaster's share of the core could be pro-rated by households. That would still be a guess, because Lancaster's household count and sales volume are not in the context provided.

## Adjacent signal: new construction

- Census permits for August 2026 show 124 units in Lancaster County. Of these, 48 were single-family and 72 were in buildings of five or more units (Census building permits).
- New-build owners are a separate audience from deed-record movers. Do not add them to the mover count.

## Caveat on the lead rate

- The 1.0% rate is an assumption. It is not a measured result.
- The week-two mail drop and the week-four read will give Punctual Pros' own response rate (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- The plan also holds out 10% of new movers, so measured leads should be read against that holdout.

## Next actions

1. Pull the last 12 months of Lancaster County deed records, filtered to arm's-length residential sales. Report the monthly count and the pre-1980 share.
2. Repeat the same split for all nine core counties. Mail volume and budget can then be allocated by county instead of across the whole core.
3. Replace the assumed 1.0% lead rate with booked jobs per piece from mail drop one. Use ServiceTitan tracking numbers and QR codes, and compare against the holdout.
4. Decide whether new-construction owners get a separate mail track. Lancaster's 48 single-family permits in August 2026 make that a small test, not a core list.
